chunks: What the Shaykh — may Allah the Exalted support him — informed me of, from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Sayf ibn ʿAmīrah, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, who said:
A number of our companions narrated to me from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “Seven buckets are to be drawn from it if a boy urinates into it, or if a mouse or the like falls into it.”
Then he said: “If an infant who has not yet eaten food urinates into it, one bucket is to be drawn from it.”
Indicated by it is the previously mentioned report of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, and that he said: “I asked him about the urine of the weaned child.” He said: “One bucket.”

Then he said — may Allah the Exalted support him: “If dry feces falls into it and does not dissolve in it nor break apart, ten buckets are to be drawn from it. If it is moist, or it dissolves and breaks apart in it, fifty buckets are to be drawn from it. And if a person in janabah immerses himself in it, purifying it by drawing seven buckets becomes obligatory.” This is indicated by it.

key_terms.الصَّبِيُّ: a young boy whose urine affects the ruling of the water
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: a person in a state requiring ghusl due to janabah
key_terms.دِلَاءٍ: buckets drawn from the water source as part of purification
key_terms.رَضِيعٌ: a nursing infant who has not yet begun eating food
key_terms.عَذِرَةٌ: feces or excrement falling into the water
key_terms.يُنْزَحُ: water is to be drawn out from a well or water source for purification

ai.seo_question: How many buckets must be drawn from a well to purify it after different kinds of impurity?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings regarding the purification of water when it is affected by various impurities. It specifies different amounts of water to be drawn depending on the type of impurity, reflecting detailed fiqh rulings on taharah and najasah in Imami hadith literature.
